newsitem.title: USA: West Coast HMOs get boost from Medicare rate.
newsitem.headline: West Coast HMOs get boost from Medicare rate.

text.p: West Coast-based health maintenance organizations got a boost on Monday from a solid rise in key Medicare payment rates, while some of their East Coast counterparts lagged.
The U.S. Health Care Finance Administration said Medicare payment rates to HMO's will rise by an average of 5.9 percent next year, compared with a 10.1 percent rise in 1996.

The rates are set for each U.S. county, and key counties in California saw rate increases between five and eight percent, while the New York City area saw a rise of zero to two percent, industry analysts said.

Cypress, Calif.-based PacifiCare Health Systems Inc said it won an overall increase of 6.1 percent for its Medicare plan, while Las Vegas-based Sierra Health Services said its increases included a 6.0 percent in southern Nevada and about 8.0 percent in the Houston area.

PacifiCare's A shares rose 1-1/4 to 79, while its B shares gained 2-1/4 to 83-3/4 in early afternoon trading. Sierra was up one to 32-1/8. Another California-based HMO, Foundation Health Corp, rose 1/8 to 30-7/8.
In a summary report, Volpe, Welty analyst Edward Keaney called the relatively small New York City increase a "major disappointment."
Oxford Health Plans, with a large portion of its business in the New York City area, was off 1-1/4 to 41-3/4.

But with only about 10 percent of U.S. elderly enrolled in managed care plans, the Medicare enrollment growth potential is more important than the premium increase, said John Penshorn at Piper Jaffray. He said he did not think the small Medicare increase would impact Oxford's earnings.
"In (Oxford's) case, the Medicare opportunity in their market is absolutely huge," Penshorn said. "I think their earnings will be fine and I think their enrollment growth will be strong."
